claims.text: The additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 HEA is a dual-nanoprecipitation alloy.
The initial alloy contains well-defined nanoprecipitates.
In situ ETEM using a high-temperature hot-stage can capture nanoprecipitate evolution during oxidation.
Concurrent EELS can capture oxidation-induced elemental redistribution in the nanoprecipitates in real time.
Nanoprecipitates evolve in size during high-temperature oxidation.
Nanoprecipitates evolve in morphology during high-temperature oxidation.
Nanoprecipitates evolve in composition during high-temperature oxidation.
High-temperature oxidizing conditions change the oxidation states of elements within the nanoprecipitates.
High-temperature oxidizing conditions change the elemental distribution within the nanoprecipitates.
ETEM coupled with EELS enables direct visualization and chemical mapping of oxidation-driven elemental partitioning.
Oxidation under the proposed ETEM conditions will produce an observable oxide layer.
Oxidation under the proposed ETEM conditions will produce measurable shifts in nanoprecipitate elemental composition.
Observing oxide formation and nanoprecipitate compositional shifts will elucidate the oxidation pathway.
Previous assessments of cast and wrought samples supplied bulk-strength data but did not resolve nanoscale elemental redistribution during oxidation.
Oxidation behavior observed in the ETEM environment may not fully represent bulk or industrial oxidation behavior.
Electron-beam exposure may introduce artifacts into the observed oxidation dynamics.
